about: Probability trees (docs/apstat-spec.md section 6). explore.scenes are the Explore view's two events (a tree's three numbers; everything else is computed by ApStatMath.probabilityTrees.joint); contexts are the Test yourself settings (ApStatMath.probabilityTrees.generate). Validator: scripts/lib/apstat-tool-checks/probability-trees.mjs.
intro: The same two events, three ways: a tree diagram, a two-way table and a Venn diagram, all linked. Pick a question and every view lights up the outcomes it counts, and, for a conditional probability, the slice it is limited to. Then simulate and watch the share of trials close in on the exact answer.
howItWorksTitle: How the three views and the simulation are built
howItWorks:
Everything comes from three numbers: P(A), P(B | A) and P(B | not A). Each path of the tree multiplies its branches (the multiplication rule), the table adds paths, and a conditional probability divides a joint probability by the probability of the condition.

  • Table. Counts out of 1,000, so a probability is a count over a total; the condition chooses which total.
  • Venn diagram. The circle areas are in proportion to P(A) and P(B), and their overlap is P(A and B), found by solving for the distance between the circles.
  • Independent means P(B | A) = P(B): the two branches to B match. Mutually exclusive means P(A and B) = 0: the circles do not touch.
  • Simulation. Each trial first draws A or not A with P(A), then B or not B with the matching conditional probability, from a seeded random number generator.

Test yourself makes new problems from a seed (the problem code), and every key is recomputed by the validator.

scenes.name: A screening test
scenes.note: A test that is right 90% of the time for sick patients still gives mostly false positives when the condition is rare: compare P(A | B) with P(B | A).

scenes.name: Sports and part-time jobs
scenes.note: Athletes are less likely to have a job here, so knowing A changes the chance of B: dependent events.

scenes.name: A spam filter
scenes.note: The word "free" is far more common in spam, so seeing it raises the chance a message is spam from 0.3 to P(A | B).

scenes.name: One roll of a fair die
scenes.note: Among the even numbers (2, 4, 6) one is a 5 or 6, and among the odd numbers (1, 3, 5) one is too: P(B | A) = P(B | not A) = 1/3, so A and B are independent.
